item.title: In 1980, conservationists began eradicating feral sheep to restore California's Santa Cruz Island
item.description: Conservationists undertook a significant effort to remove feral sheep from Santa Cruz Island, aiming to revive its delicate ecosystem. Over seven years, thousands of these sheep were eliminated, risking the extinction of a unique heritage breed. To counter this, twelve lambs were rescued to spearhead a captive breeding initiative on the mainland, ensuring the preservation of a rare genetic lineage and honoring California's rich agricultural heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Why is N3on becoming an AI streamer? Kick star defends controversial never-ending livestream
item.description: On September 7, 2026, Kick streamer N3on unveiled a groundbreaking AI streaming initiative that aims to make him the first AI streamer with an uninterrupted broadcast. This pioneering project is designed to operate continuously, even when N3on is offline. He positions this venture as an exciting evolution in content creation while reassuring fans that his traditional streaming will persist alongside this new experiment.

item.title: California town first sold on eBay in 2002, is back on market again
item.description: Bridgeville, an 80-acre town in Northern California, made history in 2002 as the first town to be listed on eBay. The auction drew 250 bids, with the highest reaching $1.77 million, but the winner backed out. After several owners and failed plans, the town is set to return to the market this September, with its current owners hoping for someone who can help the community flourish.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: As El Niño intensifies, scientists in Chile are making a vulnerable penguin species wear copper vests, here's why
item.description: In an inspiring initiative, Chilean researchers are designing specialized vests for injured penguins, incorporating copper and zinc to expedite healing. This groundbreaking effort is focused on supporting the struggling Humboldt penguin population by preventing further injury while enhancing recovery. The vests draw on effective treatments that have proven successful for domestic animals, showcasing a creative blend of technology and compassion.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Hidden gut bacteria populations linked to ageing, cancer and type 2 diabetes may spread worldwide
item.description: Scientists led by the University of Vienna have found hidden populations within common gut bacteria, some of which are linked to ageing, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease and type 2 diabetes. The study also found evidence that certain bacterial populations can spread between people and across continents within a few decades, suggesting the gut microbiome may be more transmissible and dynamic than previously thought.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Why Harry and Meghan were caught off guard by King Charles’ latest letter
item.description: King Charles III has clarified Prince Harry and Meghan's status as private citizens. The royal family confirmed they remain non-working members, which was previously agreed. This clarification came shortly before a letter was sent to senior officials. Harry and Meghan continue their commercial and charitable work in their private capacity. Their security arrangements remain a separate and ongoing discussion.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Man hid inside a Roman storage jar 1,600 years ago; archaeologists uncover his final moments
item.description: Archaeologists have unearthed the skeletal remains of a man tucked inside a massive Roman storage jar, offering a chilling glimpse into the past. It appears he sought refuge from a violent raid, as evidenced by the surrounding destruction and signs of fire. Two iron knives discovered alongside him imply a desperate act of self-defense. This city's fate remained enigmatic for an astonishing sixteen centuries before it was eventually rebuilt.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New York is building a bridge with recycled glass: $21.2 million project to divert 106 tons of glass from landfills and prevent over 72 tons of CO2 emissions
item.description: A New York bridge initiative is making headlines by incorporating recycled glass into its concrete mix. This project effectively diverts waste glass from landfills, significantly cutting down on carbon emissions. By transforming unwanted glass into a sustainable alternative for cement, this pilot demonstrates forward-thinking in construction materials. The expected completion of the project, including accompanying sidewalks, is slated for late 2026.

item.title: Texas offers $100 for invasive black carp caught near state waters
item.description: Texas offers a hundred-dollar bounty for each invasive black carp caught. This program aims to improve understanding of the species spreading through river systems. Participants can receive up to ten reimbursements monthly for collected specimens. Research focuses on the fish's age, growth, and distribution patterns. Black carp pose a threat to native freshwater mussels and snails.

item.title: Shakespeare’s Globe to replace 30-year-old roof with 14,000 reed bundles in £10m project
item.description: Shakespeare’s Globe in London is set for a major roof replacement nearly 30 years after the reconstructed theatre opened. The £10 million project will use traditional thatching and around 14,000 bundles of reed instead of modern roofing materials. The Globe’s original roof used 6,000 bundles of Norfolk reeds. The project comes as traditional thatching in England faces challenges including poor harvests, old machinery and uncertain seasonal labour supplies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: She built a 12-by-12-foot cabin with no electricity or road: The woman who chose to live alone in the Adirondack wilderness
item.description: Anne LaBastille, an iconic figure in wilderness living, constructed a secluded cabin in the Adirondack wilderness, eschewing all modern perks. Her life there was immortalized in her famous 'Woodswoman' memoir series, capturing the essence of nature. Later, her beloved property was turned over to New York State for conservation, now part of the Forest Preserve, showcasing her lasting impact in inspiring nature lovers and protecting the great outdoors.

item.title: Dubai teen built AI platform for breast cancer after losing grandmother at 10; took cancer awareness to India
item.description: Saiyette Aima’s journey began with her grandmother’s battle against breast cancer, driving her to make a significant impact. She spearheaded community-oriented fundraising and awareness campaigns, which flourished with local backing. Following this, Aima launched Pink for Purpose and started a YouTube channel to enhance her outreach. Her mission extended to India, providing free screening camps, which culminated in the innovative CareCheck, an AI tool for guiding breast health decisions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Japan’s floating solar farm faced Typhoon Faxai; modules broke loose and 50 panels caught fire
item.description: In 2019, a severe typhoon struck Japan's largest floating solar farm, leaving it heavily damaged. This event highlighted the engineering flaws present in floating solar structures when confronted with extreme weather. Investigators identified anchor failures as the main factor contributing to the significant damage. In response, the project was restructured into smaller, more resilient floating modules. Now, it serves as a reference for enhancing solar technology's storm resilience.
